cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: WSGI (PEP 3333) is the Python standard interface between a web server and a Python web app. A WSGI server like Gunicorn calls the app's application(environ, start_response) callable, so any WSGI server runs any WSGI framework such as Django or Flask.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: In production Nginx sits in front for TLS, static files and buffering slow clients. WSGI is synchronous, one request per worker; ASGI (async app(scope, receive, send)) interleaves many requests and supports WebSockets. Gunicorn is the usual default over uWSGI.

questions.q: Why put Nginx in front of Gunicorn?
questions.a: Nginx buffers slow clients, terminates TLS, serves static files, enforces limits and keeps Gunicorn off the internet.
WSGI blocks a worker per request; ASGI lets one event loop handle many requests and supports WebSockets.

questions.q: Scaling to 8 instances causes DB connection errors. Why?
questions.a: Total connections = instances x workers x pool size, now over the DB limit. Add PgBouncer or shrink pools.
